terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation: with the accusative, or without an object
evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.21: equitēs Rōmānī, quī circumstant senātum (Lewis & Short)
Verg. A. 12.85: circumstant properī aurīgae (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of people (or things) standing round someone, friendly or hostile; “very frequent and classical” (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: come and stand round, close round
terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, with the accusative
evidence: Plaut. Men. 5.7.9: quid mē circumsistitis? (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The act of gathering round, often to hem someone in; mostly in the historians, in Cicero perhaps only once (Lewis & Short). Its perfect is the same as that of circumstō.

evidence: Cic. Mil. 1: nōn enim corōnā cōnsessus vester cīnctus est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a ring of people as of a wall or a river (see surround, enclose).

phrases.english: why are you all standing round me?
the milk-white home-born slaves stand round the bright hearth
The children were standing round their grandfather, waiting for a story.

sources: Lewis & Short: circumsto · Lewis & Short: circumsisto · Lewis & Short: cingo
